verdict: BLOCKED — DO NOT DEPLOY OTA CANDIDATE v2.4.1-rc3
executive_summary: DeltaGuard correlated 10-scenario Python ctypes SIL telemetry with REA x86-64 binary disassembly of bms_v1.so and bms_v2.so. Three critical regressions were proven down to exact machine instructions and .rodata hex offsets.
audio_briefing_script: DeltaGuard Enterprise Pre-OTA Homologation Briefing. Release Gate Verdict: Candidate OTA firmware version 2.4.1 is BLOCKED due to three critical ISO 26262 and JEITA safety regressions. First, in Scenario 2 at 5 degrees Celsius, the candidate firmware appears to charge 43.7 percent faster, dropping charge time from 10,790 seconds to 6,070 seconds. However, REA binary disassembly proves the supplier stripped the 10-degree JEITA cold-weather derating branch, commanding 1.625 amps instead of 0.8125 amps and causing severe anode lithium plating. Second, in Scenario 5, the rodata thermal cutoff constant was patched from 45.0 degrees Celsius to 50.0 degrees Celsius, allowing unsafe charging to 99.7 percent State of Charge at 47 degrees. Third, in Scenario 8, the thermistor fault check is bypassed below 80 percent State of Charge, violating ISO 26262 ASIL-D single-point fault tolerance. Do not deploy bms_v2.so to the vehicle fleet until all three binary patches are verified.

correlations.standard: JEITA Li-ion Cold Charging Profile & Panasonic NCR18650B Spec
correlations.deceptive_metric: Charge duration dropped from 10790s to 6070s (-43.7% apparent speedup).
correlations.physical_anomaly: At 5.0°C ambient, Candidate v2.4.1 commands 1.625 A (0.50C) instead of the mandatory JEITA derated 0.8125 A (0.25C), driving Anode Lithium Plating Risk Index to 88.4% and depressing graphite anode potential below 0V vs Li/Li+.
correlations.binary_root_cause: REA disassembly of `<bms_step>` and `<bms_get_cold_derate_current>` in `bms_v2.so` proves that the `comiss`/`ucomiss` comparison against `10.0f` (`0x41200000`) and the `.rodata` constant `0.8125f` (`0x3F500000`) were removed, unconditionally loading `1.625f` (`0x3FD00000`).

correlations.standard: IEC 62660-2 / UN 38.3 Upper Thermal Cutoff Ceiling
correlations.deceptive_metric: Candidate v2.4.1 reaches 99.7% SoC at 47.2°C without tripping a thermal fault, whereas Baseline v1.0 safely inhibits charging (0.0 A).
correlations.physical_anomaly: Continuous 1.625 A charging at 46.5°C–47.8°C exceeds Panasonic NCR18650B's 45.0°C ceiling, accelerating SEI breakdown and cathode gas generation.
correlations.binary_root_cause: REA `.rodata` section hex diff between `bms_v1.so` and `bms_v2.so` shows IEEE-754 single-precision float `0x42340000` (`00 00 34 42` = `45.0f`) modified to `0x42480000` (`00 00 48 42` = `50.0f`).
correlations.recommended_c_patch:
/* Revert MAX_CHARGE_TEMP_LIMIT_C in .rodata to 45.0f (0x42340000) */
static const float MAX_CHARGE_TEMP_LIMIT_C = 45.0f;

correlations.scenario_id: SCEN-08 (NTC Thermistor Open-Circuit Fault at 35% SoC)
correlations.deceptive_metric: Passes high-SoC fault test (Scenario #9 at 85% SoC) while failing completely during fast-charge (Scenario #8 at 35% SoC).
correlations.physical_anomaly: When `temp_sensor_fail = 1` is injected at t = 300s (35% SoC), Baseline v1.0 opens the contactor (`0x01`) in 1 tick (1.0s), whereas Candidate v2.4.1 keeps the contactor closed (`0x00`) and drives 1.625 A blind to cell temperature.
correlations.binary_root_cause: REA control-flow disassembly of `<bms_step>` in `bms_v2.so` reveals an injected `comisd xmm2, [rip+...]` (0.80 SoC check) immediately following `test edi, edi` (`temp_sensor_fail`), bypassing the fault handler when `soc < 0.80`.
